newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani analysts say buy bellwether stocks.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani analysts say buy bellwether stocks.

text.p: Investors should build positions in Pakistan's bellwether stocks before next week's general election, according to a research report made available on Monday.

Taurus Securities said in its report investors should build positions in key stocks like PTCL (Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd) and HUBCO (Hub Power Company Ltd) at current levels in the run up to the February 3 poll.

"We think that the market will continue to rally," said the report. The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index jumped 46.86 points, or 3.27 percent, between last Tuesday's close at 1,429.63 and Sunday's finish at 1,476.49 points.
On Sunday alone, the index rose 25.08 points, or 1.73 percent.
Exchange president Arif Habib told Reuters there were several positive factors behind the rally, including a government plan to raise telephone rates and good corporate results.
Generous dividends and bonus stocks following government measures that included exempting bonus stocks from income tax, also helped, he said.
"Above all, there is some limited foreign buying interest," Habib said.

Generous dividends and bonus stocks included Saif Textile's 35 percent cash dividend for the year ended September 1996, compared to a 15 percent dividend and 10 percent bonus stocks in 1995. Nishat (Chunian) Ltd announced a 20 percent dividend against nothing in the previous year.
Dealer Salman Naqvi said a general feeling that pro-business former prime minister Nawaz Sharif would win the elections easily had lifted stock prices.
As bullish sentiment lifted prices, market capitalisation rose to 453.063 billion rupees in four trading sessions to Sunday from 444.339 billion on Tuesday.

The Taurus Securities report said the market would see the government's recent measures as largely symbolic, "but necessary for the long term growth and development of the economy and will respond favourably in the next coming weeks".
Although foreign fund managers had expressed cautious optimism, a rally based on local buying due to improved sentiment might induce foreign trading interest as well, the report said.
The market was likely to rise 100 to 150 points, but some investors were likely to adopt a wait-and-see stance until the elections, it said.
At current levels, the Pakistan market was trading at 10.3 times 1996 earnings in the financial year ending June, and 8.4 times in 1997, the report said.
"This supports our view that the market's problem at this stage is largely liquidity based," the report said.
The current low values offer investors an excellent opportunity to build up positions in the run-up to an expected post-election rally, it added.
"We maintain an overweight position in high-growth, cash-rich sectors such as fetilisers, oil marketing and independent power plants," it said.
These offer the possibility of a sharp rebound as any fresh investment inflows were likely to be focused on high-growth, liquid stocks, the report said.
